en_summary: @aleabitoreddit discusses laser players for CPO: Lightmatter CEO notes 8 optical engines/GPU is 100x more lasers. Mentions $AVGO projections, $LITE and $COHR most de-risked with long-term visibility. AI trade moves together.
text:
Just in general for laser players, from Lightmatter's CEO, regarding scale up CPO:

8 optical engines/GPU introduces 100x more lasers than scale out switching. More conservative estimates were 10x laser content from AOI's CFO. 

Along with ASPs for those lasers going higher (eg. 10x ASPs than pluggables for single emitter UHP lasers).

From what I've seen yearly capacity expansion for lasers generally increase around ~3x Y/Y like $AVGO projections, or ~5x over 2-3 years like Furukawa's. 

This is what I mean by optical content like lasers + requirements (more InP substrates), rises per generation and bottlenecks on UHP ranges might persist through 2030 despite aggregate capex decreasing.

Which is what I'm trying to argue here. 

Future CPO laser competitors like Furukawa/AOI/Shija are more nuanced, since AOI is focused on 800G/1.6T transceivers (which faced capacity expansion delays + DSP Bottlenecks), but they have capability for 400mW+ ranges + ongoing CPO qualifications. 

I don't think transceivers have the same durability though in capex reduction scenarios, which is why I've been arguing the valuable optionality AOI has to focus on merchant lasers is mispriced. 

A lot of it is execution/qualification rather than demand, $LITE + $COHR are the most de-risked with confirmed long term visibility. 

But entire AI trade is moving up and down together.

BofA Securities kept its Buy rating on $TSM with a price objective of $620 per share, 55% above the $398 price at publication. 

The note focuses on Arizona: a new long-term power contract that lifts the site's electricity supply to 1.88 GW, enough in BofA's estimate to triple advanced-node capacity, and evidence that the US fabs are profitable even before government grants.

The numbers behind BofA's estimate:

- Power: TSMC and Arizona Public Service signed a long-term agreement that extends electricity service to 1.88 GW at full buildout, up from 1.2 GW. Because TSMC makes an upfront credit-support payment in January 2027, APS treats the full 1.88 GW as committed demand and could supply more. 

- Capacity: At about 10 MW per 1,000 wafers a month of advanced-node capacity, plus some power for back-end packaging, BofA estimates the site could reach ~150k wafers a month, against ~50k by Q4 2027. That is roughly three times the 2027 level. 

- Revenue: At the current build cadence this could be in place by 2035, before the additional facilities announced earlier this year, and generate more than $60bn of revenue a year. For scale, BofA expects TSMC's total revenue to be about $176bn in 2026.

Bitcoin mining software firm Luxor hacked: attackers steal 0.243 $BTC in rewards from miners

"In case you're wondering, what Luxor does is they make software that lets Bitcoin miners manage their machines. So it's not doing the mining, it's the software that does the management."

"Attackers were able to compromise that software, apparently using AI, and changed where the machines sent their mining work. So the miners kept paying for the electricity and doing the actual mining, but the attacker collected the Bitcoin rewards, which were sent to their wallet."

"It wasn't a huge amount, but again, another novel attack surface that nobody had seen coming for crypto-related software, and it becomes absolutely exhausting."

"So far this is only 0.243 Bitcoin. But if you're mining Bitcoin or looking at Bitcoin miners or using software that's related to it, now you have to be worried about that as well."

"The miners got the electricity bill for it, but the hacker got the direct deposit."

Elon Musk reveals he recruited SpaceX’s first engineers by telling them 'we’re probably going to die', and ended up as chief engineer because no good one would join

“So SpaceX, I started that in mid-2002 expecting to fail. Probably 90% chance of failing.”

“And even when recruiting people, I didn’t try to make out that it would work. I said, we’re probably going to die, but there’s a small chance we might not die, and this is the only way to get people to Mars and advance the state of the art.”

“And then I ended up being chief engineer of the rocket, not because I wanted to, but because I couldn’t hire anyone who was good. None of the good chief engineers would join, because they’re like, this is too risky, you’re going to die. And so I ended up being chief engineer of the rocket.”

我最新的產業調查與研究結論：

1. 訂單能見度與出貨規劃：
受惠於 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 強勁新訂單，Google TPU 出貨能見度已達 2029 年，優於 Nvidia GPU 與其他 AI ASIC（多數為 4Q27–2Q28）。

(1) 自 2028 年起，v9 將成 Google 自建算力的主力方案，v8 系列（8t／8i 或其設計變種）訂單可視為來自 OpenAI 與 Anthropic。

(2) 2028–2029 年合計需求數量：OpenAI 約 12M（聯發科設計的 8t），Anthropic 約 14M（Broadcom 設計的 8i），兩者需求均呈逐年成長趨勢。OpenAI 採買斷，Anthropic 則是租賃與買斷都有。

(3) 考量供應鏈限制，2027–2029 年較合理的 TPU 出貨估算分別為 8–9M、14–15M、16–18M。市場普遍預期 AI 資本支出於 2028 年見頂，但此規劃顯示 TPU 在 2029 年仍具出貨成長動能，關鍵在於 AI 服務龍頭 OpenAI 與 Anthropic 的直接訂單。

2. v10 產品線與供應鏈調整：
v10 由原先的 Icefish 與 Merope／Bladerunner 改為 Quillfish，預計 2029 年量產，設計服務訂單由聯發科取得。

(1) Icefish 改為 v11，預計 2030 年量產，設計服務訂單同由聯發科取得。Merope 能見度較低，供應商未定，也可能取消。

(2) 聯發科將是 v9（Humufish & Triggerfish）與 v10（Quillfish）的獨家供應商，2027–2029 年占整體 TPU 供應比重分別約 45–50%、50–55%、55–60%。TPU 對其營收與利潤的貢獻預計逐年增加。

(3) 自 v9 起新款 TPU 均採 Intel EMIB-T 先進封裝。考量初期量產能力，預期至 2029 年仍以 v8 系列為 TPU 出貨主力。v8 預期將是聯發科與 Broadcom 未來數年的 TPU 事業獲利成長的主要來源，因長期累積的學習曲線效益明顯，加上雙方負責關鍵零組件與材料採購。
